_comment: Machine-readable form of docs/PROJECT-CLOSURE-GATE.md (APPROVED 2026-09-14). The .md is authoritative prose; this file is what `aisef closure` evaluates. `contract_sha256` pins the .md: if it changes, closure is STALE. Probes name callables already in the package wherever one exists, so the gate reads through the SAME reader the product uses.

severity_scale._comment: Reused, not redefined. P0 = cannot install, data loss, security issue, incorrect gate result. P1 = cannot complete lifecycle without author assistance.

criteria.statement: the released tag, HEAD, and the frozen closure target are one revision
criteria.notes: Owner adjustment 2 (2026-09-14). G1 certified the PyPI artefact at the tag commit while G2-G5 read HEAD, measured 46 commits apart -- different software combined into one record. One criterion owns the invariant so the failure names both revisions in one place; two conjuncts (tag resolves to the target, HEAD is still the target) and it must not pass on one of them. An unset target is UNRUNNABLE, never a pass: nothing to compare is not agreement. Set with `aisef closure --pin-target` on the candidate, which refuses on a dirty tree.

criteria.statement: CI is green on the commit the released tag points at
wheel and sdist build, and twine check passes both
a clean venv install from PyPI serves the released version
runtime package data ships inside the wheel and is non-empty
the full test suite is green, run from the MAIN checkout
criteria.notes: UNRUNNABLE if not the main working tree: a git worktree skips ~61 more tests because .gitignore excludes references/*, .bench*/, .conformance/, .dogfood/. The probe records the skip count and the tree it ran in.

criteria.statement: the lint gate is clean under the rule set in pyproject.toml
zero OPEN P0/P1 defects in the canonical register
no known false PASS in a deterministic or structural blocking check
a judge-only block is identifiable, distinguishable, overridable, and cannot masquerade as deterministic
criteria.notes: Owner ruling 1. The four properties are G2.4b-i..iv in the contract. A WAIVED outcome requires an explicit owner reason; the measured rate (miss 34-39%, 11 of 20 same-tree reversals, 36.8% judge-alone blocks) stays published and recomputable.

criteria.statement: every first-class client has a complete, passing conformance column
criteria.notes: Reads through conformance.release_ready, which must require both claude and opencode (ADR-006 §4). Owner ruling 5: no re-run merely to refresh a still-valid timestamp; the report prints days remaining.

corpus._comment: Owner ruling 2. Fallback admissible ONLY for an external/environmental block, never for an unresolved AISEF defect, and only as a named R1 substitution the owner approves.

criteria.statement: the corpus is resolvable by path and has an artifact root
every upstream human gate is APPROVED and not STALE
every planned story reached done, and none was never run
independent review and security ran for every story
deterministic verification is recorded at the merged candidate, not a stale one
pre-deploy passes with its scope declared
criteria.notes: Only the isolation sub-check is waiver-eligible, via the existing sandbox.pre_deploy_degraded_waiver with its reason. Docker availability is an environment fact.

criteria.statement: the PRE_DEPLOY gate is human-approved against THAT report
criteria.notes: aisef closure must never approve this.

criteria.statement: the methodology was pre-registered before any column-2 data existed, and its digest still matches

prereg_frozen_region._comment: Owner ruling 7. The digest covers ONLY the frozen region -- the verbatim pre-registration -- not the whole file, so a dated addendum outside the markers does not break the pin while any edit inside it does. It is recorded HERE and nowhere inside the file it pins: a digest living in its own subject is updated in the same motion as the text and pins nothing. `also_in` is the pre-data commit carrying the same bytes; the same recipe must yield the same digest there, and that equality is what dates the text. Verify: docs/BENCH-PREREGISTRATION-C2.md section 1.1.
prereg_frozen_region.normalise: CRLF and CR -> LF; strip leading and trailing blank lines of the region; nothing else -- byte-exact inside. Deliberately UNLIKE onboarding_digest: that one normalises content because a typo fix must not invalidate a person's validation; this one must break on a typo fix, because the value it protects is that the text never changes.

criteria.notes: Owner ruling 7. Prediction and success criteria are never rewritten after data exists.

criteria.statement: cut sessions are not silently mixed with valid ones
a model-CLI pair whose cut-session behaviour satisfies the pre-registered validity rule has been established

protocol_frozen_region._comment: Owner adjustment 4 (2026-09-14): the qualification protocol is frozen and pinned BEFORE any real session runs -- 'do not inspect qualification results and then choose the threshold'. Same recipe as prereg_frozen_region, different markers, and recorded HERE rather than inside the document it pins. The frozen region carries all nine declared items and the arithmetic that derives the threshold, so a later reader can see the bar predates the data. Section 2.10 of the region restates every constant; tests/bench/_qualify.py is its code copy and the reference check asserts they match, so changing a threshold without re-freezing the text turns the suite red.
protocol_frozen_region.normalise: CRLF and CR -> LF; strip leading and trailing blank lines of the region; nothing else -- byte-exact inside, exactly like prereg_frozen_region and for the same reason.

criteria.notes: Owner ruling 3: not waived pre-emptively. States WAIVER_PENDING when no available pair qualifies; the 72-attempt run does not start until PASSED. Adjustment 4: no real qualification session may run before protocol_sha256 above is recorded.

criteria.statement: benchmark evidence is reproducible: dataset digest matches and selfcheck passes
noise and inconclusive results are reported as such
no unreproducible historical claim is presented as current evidence
the validation report exists at the path the protocol declares, carrying the protocol's metric fields
criteria.notes: docs/EXTERNAL-VALIDATION-v1.1.0.md is the PROTOCOL, not the record. Its existence does not satisfy this.

criteria.statement: the participant is a genuinely external person, not an AI agent and not an AISEF contributor
criteria.notes: Owner ruling 4. Not machine-decidable on its own; the probe checks the record asserts it and the owner confirms at approval.

criteria.statement: no unresolved P0/P1 onboarding blocker

onboarding_digest._comment: Owner ruling 4. Deterministic hash over the PUBLIC ONBOARDING SURFACE only, taken over extracted and normalised content (whitespace collapsed, prose reflow ignored) -- never raw file bytes, because a typo fix must not invalidate a real person's validation.

_evidence_note: G1.* and G5.4's selfcheck half read recorded verifications (closure-evidence/release.json, closure-evidence/bench-selfcheck.json) because the evaluator is read-only: resolving them live would mean a network call, a build and an install. The CI record is cross-checked against the tag's real commit locally so it cannot self-assert.

exit_codes._note: Deliberately NOT the rest of this CLI's convention (1 usage / 2 not-ready). The contract §4.3 specified these numbers; an unrecognised flag is still reported by the top-level parser and exits 1, as for every verb.
